subject: Clarify route-slice definitions + exception handling for console drilldown
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Nguyen <alex@scaleops.io>, Samir Patel <samir@stellarapps.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify route-slice definitions + exception handling for console drilldown

Hi team,

As promised in the product-obs sync, I'm opening a short thread to capture a few outstanding questions from StellarApps' QA run and to align on an exception plan we can present in the customer workshop next week. They hit a confusing UX when a tenant's route surface spans multiple "slices" (short/long context + embeddings calls) and the console currently shows separate cost/latency rows that look like independent endpoints.

Quick asks:
- Can we define a deterministic rule we can display in the console tooltip that maps a request to a single "route slice" for attribution? (e.g., primary model + first-token-length bucket)
- If a route is split across slices at runtime (KV cache hit for part of the flow), what should the console do visually? Collapse into a single row with a badge, or show the split but link them?
- For SLA/exceptioning: if a tenant hits a high tail latency on the long-context slice but normal on the short slice, do we trigger a route-level SLA, or slice-level? Stellar wants predictable alerting and an action plan.

I've attached: console-prototype-v2.png (mock with a proposed badge) and a small telemetry export from their test run that highlights the split flows.

My suggested approach (for discussion):
1) Attribution rule: map to "owner route" by canonical route id + dominant model in the call. If split, attribute to the route and expose slice breakdown under an expandable row.
2) UX: single row with a chevron to expand slice rows; include a small "split" badge and hover text.
3) SLA: treat SLA at route-level by default; allow customers to opt into slice-level alerts when they are running mixed pipelines.

Next steps: Jonas, can you confirm whether the backend telemetry supports stable canonical route id in all cases? Marissa, can you weigh in on console affordances and how much real estate we have for expansion?

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Product Management – Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Nguyen <alex@scaleops.io>, Samir Patel <samir@stellarapps.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify route-slice definitions + exception handling for console drilldown

Irene — thanks for laying this out. Quick answers from runtime/telemetry perspective:

- We currently generate a canonical route id for every incoming request (route_id) at the API gateway. That id survives batching and forwarding, so attribution by route_id is safe.
- The problem is when a single logical request fans out to two model calls (embedding lookup + long-form generation) — we emit separate spans with different model tags. We do tag both spans with the original route_id, though, so joining is possible.
- Memory: the existing storage schema keeps per-span model and token counts; we can easily add an "is_primary_model" flag during ingest if the product wants a dominance heuristic computed at write-time.

Operational implication: joining by route_id and presenting slice rows under an expandable parent row is feasible without a new schema. We'll need a short ingest-side transform to set the dominance flag for UX convenience. Cost: ~2 engineer-weeks (telemetry team) to ship ingest transform and backfill tooling.

For SLA semantics, I agree with route-level default. Slice-level as opt-in is reasonable but we should define the opt-in contract (boolean per tenant + per-route override).

I'll schedule a quick sync with infra and telemetry owners if we want to commit this quarter.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Engineering Manager, Serving Platform

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Nguyen <alex@scaleops.io>, Samir Patel <samir@stellarapps.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify route-slice definitions + exception handling for console drilldown

Thanks — this is helpful. A few notes from Console/UX:

- Expandable parent row + linked slice rows is our preferred pattern (keeps dashboards tidy and surfaces detail on demand). The split badge is good, but let's avoid anything that looks like a new primary metric.
- We should add a compact legend and an inline copy block (hover / info) that explains the attribution rule in plain language: "Metrics are attributed to the canonical route; slices show per-call breakdowns (embedding vs. generation)." That copy needs legal/CS sign-off before we ship to a customer.
- Action items for us:
  * I'll mock a compact legend and update the sample image (attach v2 -> v2a) and share in the drive link.
  * Product copy: Irene, can you draft the short help text? I'll send to legal/CS after review.

On SLA UX: route-level SLA with an "enable slice alerts" toggle in tenant settings seems straightforward. That toggle should create a per-tenant alert rule in the monitor service (we'll need telemetry to expose slice metrics via the monitor API).

I'll add two small tickets to the Console backlog: CON-1347 (UX mock + copy) and CON-1348 (tenant toggle + settings page). Estimated effort: 1.5 PM weeks + 1 Eng week for frontend work to render expandable rows.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Console & Observability

From: Samir Patel <samir@stellarapps.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify route-slice definitions + exception handling for console drilldown

Irene / team — thanks for the clear plan and the quick responses. The sample telemetry we sent shows the route_id on both spans; having the console collapse to the canonical route then expand into slices will solve most of our confusion. Two quick asks from our side: 

1) Can we get a short blurb (one paragraph) that we can paste into our internal runbook that describes the default SLA behavior?
2) If you proceed with the dominance flag, please let us know the timeline — we want to re-run the QA once that's in so the console displays the right highlight.

Happy to join the sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
SRE Lead, StellarApps
Attachments: sample-telemetry-export.csv
